study.title: Modulations of static and dynamic functional connectivity among brain networks by electroacupuncture in post-stroke aphasia
study.study_design: Task-based fMRI study with block design; two-group (PSA patients vs. healthy controls) within-subject comparison of EA stimulation vs. rest at baseline
study.population: 19 patients with post-stroke aphasia (PSA) and 16 demographically matched healthy volunteers (HCs); 35 right-handed participants recruited between August 2013 and February 2021
study.disease_condition: Post-stroke aphasia (PSA) caused by left hemisphere stroke
study.inclusion_criteria: Patients with PSA were recruited from the Department of Neurology at Dongzhimen Hospital with complaints of language disorders. Healthy controls (HCs) were recruited from the local community. All participants were right-handed.

arms.dropouts: 3 excluded due to excessive head movement; 4 excluded due to incomplete information for CRRCAE correlation

conditions.scan_context: task-based fMRI block design; rest blocks alternating with stimulation blocks

conditions.timepoint_exact: 30-s stimulation period within block design; 6 stimulation blocks
conditions.scan_context: task-based fMRI block design; EA delivered during scan at HT5 and GB39

interventions.procedure_label_exact: electroacupuncture stimulation at HT5 and GB39
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: HT5: radially to the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon on the anteromedial side of the forearm, 33 mm proximal to the palmar wrist crease. GB39: 100 mm above the external malleolus tip, on the anterior fibula border.
interventions.manipulation_exact: EA technique; Han's acupoint nerve stimulator (model LH202H)
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: All participants reported their experience ('Deqi') with acupuncture stimulation. Deqi featured aching, pressure, heaviness, fullness, and numbness among other feelings.
interventions.session_duration_exact: 6 min total scan (12 blocks of 30 s each)
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Tongli (HT5) and Xuanzhong (GB39) are important language-implicated acupoints used in Chinese medicine. They are commonly used in PSA rehabilitation therapy because they are tailored to language-processing systems.

neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: T1: isotropic multi-echo magnetization-prepared rapid acquisition sequence. Functional: single shot gradient-recalled echo planar imaging sequence (31 interleaved axial slices)

neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: Statistical Parametric Mapping 12 software suite (SPM12); Resting-State fMRI Data Analysis Toolkit (REST plus, version 1.24)
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: 6-mm Gaussian kernel with full width at half maximum (FWHM)
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: All data had head motions <3 mm or 3°; 3 participants excluded due to excessive head movement
statistical_thresholds_exact: For correlation analyses: p-value < 0.05 with no corrections for multiple comparisons
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: false discovery rate (FDR) correction; positive false discovery rate (pFDR)

extraction_notes.note: Supplementary Table 1 referenced for full list of nine network components and temporal properties details. Content not provided in the main PDF.
Supplementary Figure 1 referenced for ROI locations derived from previous multi-voxel pattern analysis (MVPA) results. Coordinates and definitions for 23 ROIs not provided in the main PDF.
Supplementary Figure S2 referenced for 12 Dyn-ICA circuit components at the network level. Component outlines not viewable in the main PDF.
Supplementary Figure S3 referenced for 12 Dyn-ICA circuit components at the ROI level. Component outlines not viewable in the main PDF.

No sham or placebo control condition was included in this study. All participants (both PSA and HC) received real EA stimulation. The comparison is between PSA and HC groups and between EA stimulation vs. rest at baseline.
Expectancy, credibility, blinding success, and allocation guessing were not reported or assessed in this study.
Adverse events were not reported in this study.

The second MNI coordinate for the Lingual gyrus in Table 3 (Group × condition interaction effect row) is listed as Calcarine L (-3 -93 11) to Lingual R (12 -39 0). The coordinate for the Lingual gyrus is only extractable from Table 3 as listed in the 'Regions' columns.

The F-values in Table 2 (spatial map of SN) are reported as negative (e.g., -3.92, -4.45, -4.00), but the text states 'PSA group showed activated clusters...compared to the HC group.' The negative sign in F-values may reflect the directionality coding in the CONN toolbox rather than deactivation. Preserved as reported.

The pFDR for circuit3 variability in Table 4 reads 0.034 in the table but the abstract/text states pFDR = 0.036 for one of the spatial connections (middle cingulum and PostCG). These are separate measures (temporal vs. spatial); extracted separately as reported.
Table 4 lists the pFDR for circuit3 frequency spatial result (SMG – Posterior cingulum) as 0.031, but the abstract states pFDR = 0.03. Both values preserved as reported in their respective locations.

The Middle temporal gyrus coordinate for the PSA EA stimulation > rest contrast (Table 3) is MNI: 52 -4 -20 (right). This coordinate is listed as the second region in the same row as Precentral L (-44 -9 41) in Table 3. Extracted as a network edge linking the two regions.

The r-value for 'command describing score' correlation (Figure 5G label shows r = -0.7, p = 0.12) conflicts with the text which states uncorrected p = 0.011 for command describing score. Figure 5G appears to show a non-significant result (p = 0.12) while the text reports significance. These may refer to different subscales. The figure label for G says 'Command describing' with p = 0.12 (non-significant). The text refers to 'command describing score (uncorrected p = 0.011)'. This inconsistency is preserved; text-reported values were used for extraction.

The n_analyzed for correlation analyses is inferred as 12 based on the statement that 4 PSA participants were excluded due to incomplete information, leaving n = 12 for CRRCAE correlation analyses (from the flow diagram).

The Figure 5 caption labels A as 'Changes in temporal properties varies of circuit1' and B as 'Spatial map of circuit1 for the contrast of condition main effect,' but the text and Table 4 confirm these correspond to the network-level Dyn-ICA results. This is consistent with the extraction.
No trial registration number was reported. The ethics approval reference number ECPJ-BDY-2015-04 is available but no prospective registration in a clinical trials database was mentioned.
Deqi sensation was described qualitatively (aching, pressure, heaviness, fullness, numbness) but no quantitative deqi scales, scores, or subscale ratings were reported.

The coordinate listed for the Orbital superior frontal gyrus connection in Table 3 (PSA EA > rest) gives coordinates for Precentral L (-44 -9 41) as the seed region, and Orbital superior frontal R (14 55 -17) as the target. The F-value -3.35 corresponds to this pair. The Middle temporal gyrus R (52 -4 -20) connection F = -4.03 is listed in the same row block, both with Precentral L as seed.
